title: api: versioned request/response schemas with beta headers and backcompat shims
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: As we add structured-output, tool/function-calling ergonomics, and OpenAI-compat shims we need a controlled, discoverable way to evolve request/response shapes without breaking existing clients. This PR introduces first-class API schema versioning with opt-in beta headers and lightweight backward-compatibility shims on the server. Goals: 1) Allow new fields and shape changes behind an opt-in header so SDKs and customers can migrate on their cadence; 2) Keep default behavior stable for current clients (no change unless header set); 3) Provide server-side shims for the most common backwards-compat mappings to reduce customer friction; 4) Surface deprecations clearly in responses and docs.

Summary of changes (single-line narrative): add version negotiation middleware, support X-Redwood-API-Version and Accept vendor headers, introduce v2 request/response proto/json schemas for chat/streaming/structured-output, implement backcompat shims for OpenAI compatibility layer, mark legacy fields as deprecated and emit deprecation warnings in responses when header opts into newer schema.

Implementation notes: - Version negotiation: header X-Redwood-API-Version: "2025-11-01" or vendor Accept header like "application/vnd.redwood.v2+json" selects the v2 schema path. If absent, server defaults to v1 behavior. - Beta header semantics: when client sets X-Redwood-API-Version to any date >= 2025-11-01 we treat it as opt-in to schema v2 beta and enable experimental structured-output tokenization and stricter validation. - Backcompat shims: server maps new v2 fields to v1 equivalents in the response body when the client does not opt-in; when mutually requested (v2 client to v1 server) the compatibility layer in openai-compat will translate requests. Common shims implemented: structured "response.blocks" -> legacy "choices[*].message/content"; function_call.{name,arguments} -> tools[] with a unified payload; streaming chunk envelope now includes both legacy "delta" and new "fragment" keys for phased rollout. - Deprecations: legacy top-level "model_params" renamed to "model_config" in v2. Deprecated keys continue to be emitted under a compat flag but include an "X-Redwood-Deprecation" response header with guidance.

Migration guidance (for SDKs and customers): 1) Try beta header: curl -H "X-Redwood-API-Version: 2025-11-01" to opt-in and check new schema. 2) Update your deserializers to prefer v2 shapes but fall back to legacy fields. 3) For streaming clients, handle both legacy "delta" chunks and new "fragment" envelopes. 4) To keep using OpenAI-compatible client code, use the redwood-openai-compat shim which translates OpenAI-style function calling into the new structured-output format; we ship updated python/ts SDK examples. 5) Remove reliance on deprecated fields after monitoring deprecation headers; full removal planned in 2026-Q2 (TBD in separate deprecation RFC).

Testing and rollout: - Unit and integration tests added for negotiation, shim translations, and streaming envelopes. - E2E test against the openai-compat adapter included. - Canary rollout: feature flag gate allows enabling beta headers on a small percentage of requests and individual customer toggle for Dedicated.

Compatibility trade-offs and performance: shims add negligible CPU overhead on common fast-paths but introduce an additional serialization step for complex function-call translations (~0.3ms median per request in benchmarks). We added an internal perf toggle to bypass shims for enterprise customers who prefer manual migration.

Docs and visibility: updated API reference (docs/api/versioning.md), examples in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript, and release notes included below. Response deprecation headers and a new /v1/compatibility/warnings endpoint give programmatic visibility for clients.

Checklist: - [x] Add negotiation middleware and header parsing - [x] Add v2 proto/json schemas for chat, streaming, structured-output - [x] Implement common backcompat shims in openai-compat and server-side adapters - [x] Update SDK examples and docs - [x] Add tests and CI jobs - [x] Add release notes and migration guide
commits: feat(api): add version negotiation middleware and header parsing
feat(schema): add v2 json/proto schemas for chat, streaming, structured-output
feat(compat): implement backcompat shims for OpenAI compatibility layer
docs: add versioning and migration guide to docs/api/versioning.md
test: add unit & e2e tests for negotiation and shim translations
chore(sdk): update python/ts examples for v2 beta header
review_conversation: Derek Liu: Nice approach. Two asks: 1) add a short-circuit config to disable shims entirely for Dedicated customers; 2) add a perf benchmark to CI to catch regressions.
Asha Patel: Added enterprise bypass flag and added a perf microbenchmark under tests/perf/versioning_benchmark. Thanks for the catch.
Priya Menon: API surface looks good. Please ensure SDK deserializers prefer new fields and fallback to legacy keys. Also requested clearer examples for streaming changes.
Asha Patel: Updated SDK examples and added streaming client snippet showing handling of 'delta' and 'fragment' envelopes.
Ethan Zhao: Found one minor race in streaming re-assembly when both envelopes are present; added fix and test. Approving after green CI.
CI: initial run had a flaky test (tests/streams/test_reassembly) — rerun passed.
Derek Liu: Approved. Priya Menon: Approved. Ethan Zhao: Approved.
release_notes: Introduce API schema versioning. Opt-in beta headers (X-Redwood-API-Version and vendor Accept) enable v2 structured response shapes.
Server provides compatibility shims for common OpenAI compatibility mappings to ease migration.
Legacy fields are deprecated and a response header 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' will include guidance when opting into newer schemas.
SDK examples updated for Python/TypeScript to demonstrate migration patterns.
